name: Ocular Cystinosis

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic cystine crystal deposits in the cornea detected by slit-lamp examination
Elevated cystine levels in leukocytes or other nucleated cells confirmed by biochemical assay
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the CTNS gene by molecular genetic testing
Positive family history of cystinosis or related symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of corneal cystine crystals plus either elevated cystine levels in leukocytes or identification of CTNS gene mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biochemical and genetic testing.

laboratory: Elevated cystine concentration in leukocytes (>0.2 nmol half-cystine/mg protein)
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing corneal cystine crystals
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) may show corneal deposits
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Delayed growth and renal tubular dysfunction in systemic forms

distinguishingFeatures: Calcium deposition in cornea rather than cystine crystals
Associated with hypercalcemia or chronic ocular inflammation
Different patterns of corneal deposits without systemic cystine accumulation
Lack of elevated cystine levels in leukocytes
Glycogen accumulation rather than cystine crystals

redFlags: Early onset photophobia with corneal crystal deposits
Progressive visual impairment in a child
references: Gahl WA, Thoene JG, Schneider JA. Cystinosis. N Engl J Med. 2002;347(2):111-121.
Nesterova G, Gahl WA. Cystinosis: the evolution of a treatable disease. Pediatr Nephrol. 2013;28(1):51-59.
Orphanet: Ocular cystinosis. Orphanet Report Series. 2024.
